name: Pocket Dimension
description: Granular multi-effect that turns a loaded picture into the XY surface for time-stretching, with a flying UFO that modulates parameters on its own.
whyUnique: The interface is an image you load yourself, and the modulation is a little spaceship. Nothing else in this list works like that.
bitwigTips: Map Bitwig's Macro knobs to the XY parameters, then add a Random modulator to push it further than the built-in UFO does.

name: Mishby
description: An unstable degradation box: auto-glitching, frequency shifting and wobbly tape wow, all built to sound like it is about to fall apart.
whyUnique: Most lo-fi plugins aim for nostalgia. Mishby aims for chaos, and the randomness is part of the design.
bitwigTips: Put it in an FX Layer at partial mix, or on a Return with Bitwig's Dry/Wet, so the chaos sits beside the clean signal.

name: Backmask
description: Reverses snippets of incoming audio, triggered by input level, tempo sync or pure chance.
whyUnique: Chance-triggered reversal on a live signal, as opposed to manually reversing clips.
bitwigTips: Try it on a drum bus with probability-triggered reversals. It pairs nicely with Bitwig's own note-probability.

name: Palindrome
description: Four-sampler granular instrument with a vector XY grid. You draw custom paths that the playheads follow while morphing between the four sources.
whyUnique: You design the movement itself, as drawn paths across four sounds, instead of only setting static grain parameters.
bitwigTips: Drag four contrasting clips from the Bitwig browser into the slots, then let Bitwig's Step modulator drive path speed.

name: Fracture
description: Free buffer-based glitch effect: stutters, repeats and filtered artifacts.
whyUnique: A long-standing free glitch tool with a sound that is easy to recognize. A good first stop before paying for anything.
bitwigTips: Pair it with Hysteresis (also free) in a Chain, and switch the chain on and off with a Button modulator.

name: Hysteresis
description: Free glitch delay with stutter, filter and modulation in the feedback path.
whyUnique: A delay that mangles every repeat a little more.
bitwigTips: Automate the mix with Bitwig 6's new automation curve shapes for swells of glitch.

name: Granite
description: Granular synth for evolving pads and atmospheres. Motion recorders let you draw freehand modulation, and cycle modulators move individual grains.
whyUnique: Per-grain modulation gives the sound internal movement that whole-voice LFOs can't produce.
bitwigTips: Long evolving pads sit well on a Bitwig Note FX chain with the Arpeggiator set to slow, wide gates.

name: crusher-X
description: Deep real-time granular processor that can run multichannel and is aimed at live processing.
whyUnique: One of the few granular tools built around live and multichannel input instead of loaded samples.
bitwigTips: Route a live input track into it and record the result with Bitwig's audio receiver on another track.

name: Portal
description: Musical granular effect with a big circular XY pad that blends many parameters at once. It handles time-stretching, pitch and tempo-synced grain delay.
whyUnique: Fairly well known, but it's the most immediate way into granular sound. Featured in the source overview.
bitwigTips: Map the XY puck to an Expressions or Keytrack modulator so the velocity of each note moves the texture.

name: SpaceCraft Granular Synth
description: Desktop version of the cult iOS granular synth: drop in any sample and play clouds polyphonically.
whyUnique: Started life as a mobile app. Its simple, tactile granular approach carried over to the desktop.
bitwigTips: Bounce a Bitwig clip, drop the file in, and play it back as a pad in the same project.

name: ++spectral bundle (++morphfilter)
description: Classic FFT spectral shapers. ++morphfilter smoothly morphs between two filter shapes using LFO or automation.
whyUnique: Experimental spectral DSP from Tom Erbe, a pioneer of the field, and still free.
bitwigTips: Drive the morph from Bitwig's Audio Sidechain modulator so another track sculpts the spectrum.

name: MSpectralDynamics
description: Compression, expansion and gating per frequency bin.
whyUnique: Dynamics in the spectral domain can isolate tones, scrub noise or turn sustained parts into ghostly versions of themselves.
bitwigTips: Use extreme expansion on a resampled vocal for spectral 'freeze' effects.

name: MORPH
description: Real-time structural morphing between two audio signals, such as a voice turning into strings.
whyUnique: True morphing (not crossfading) between two live sources.
bitwigTips: Feed the second input from another track through the plugin's sidechain input in Bitwig.

name: PaulXStretch
description: Extreme time-stretching (the Paulstretch algorithm) as a plugin. It turns seconds into hours of drone.
whyUnique: Stretches far past what normal time-stretching can do, into pure ambient smear.
bitwigTips: Render the output to a clip, then chop it with Bitwig's Sampler in Grains mode.

name: Multipass
description: Multiband host for Kilohearts snapins, with modulation per band.
whyUnique: A modular multiband rack inside one plugin.
bitwigTips: Bitwig's own Multiband FX-3 covers the basics. Use Multipass when you want snapins per band.

name: ShaperBox 3 (TimeShaper, etc.)
description: Drawn-curve effects for time, volume, filter, pan, noise and more. TimeShaper draws stutters, tape stops and halftime directly.
whyUnique: You draw the time manipulation itself as a curve.
bitwigTips: Bitwig's Curves and Segments modulators do some of this natively. ShaperBox is faster for time effects.

name: Effectrix 2
description: Step-sequenced multi-effect: paint loops, scratches, reverses and stretches onto a grid.
whyUnique: A sequencer for effects instead of notes. The grid makes rhythmic glitching fast.
bitwigTips: It syncs to Bitwig's transport. Use clip launcher scenes with different Effectrix patterns.

name: Emergent Drums 2
description: AI drum generator that creates new one-shot drum samples and variations of your own samples.
whyUnique: Generates drum hits that never existed instead of pulling them from a library.
bitwigTips: Drag generated hits into a Bitwig Drum Machine and keep the ones that work.

name: Synplant 2
description: Grow synth patches like plants. Genopatch analyzes an audio sample and tries to breed a patch that sounds like it.
whyUnique: Audio-to-patch resynthesis through an organic, botanical interface.
bitwigTips: Resample a texture in Bitwig and drag it into Genopatch to get a playable synth version.

name: Microtonic
description: Synthesized drum machine with a built-in pattern sequencer and morphing between patches.
whyUnique: Every drum is synthesized, and the morph slider blends entire kits.
bitwigTips: Route MIDI from Bitwig clips to override the internal sequencer, or use the internal patterns as a performance tool.

name: Derailer
description: Physical-modeling synth of strings, bars and springs, played by realistic and impossible exciters.
whyUnique: Models physical objects to create sounds that don't exist in the real world.
bitwigTips: Bitwig 6 supports MPE well. Use a polyphonic expression controller to drive the excitation.

name: Modus
description: MPE physical-modeling synth of connected strings and plates. Recent versions accept sidechain audio as an exciter.
whyUnique: Using external audio to excite modeled strings and plates turns it into a physical-modeling effect.
bitwigTips: Send a drum loop into Modus's sidechain to make it 'ring' through virtual plates.

name: Pivot
description: Synth from FORS, the studio known for experimental Max for Live devices. The CLAP build supports pitch bend through CLAP note expressions.
whyUnique: Comes from a small experimental studio, and it's one of the few in this list with a confirmed CLAP build.
bitwigTips: Load the CLAP version so Bitwig can send per-note expressions and modulate parameters per voice.

name: Airwindows Consolidated
description: Hundreds of quirky Airwindows algorithms (500+ as of 2026) in one CLAP-native plugin with built-in docs.
whyUnique: A huge library of odd, one-purpose processors, each with its own tiny idea.
bitwigTips: Load the CLAP version and browse algorithms while Bitwig keeps every parameter modulatable.

name: CHOW Tape Model
description: Physically modeled analog tape (hysteresis, wow and flutter, loss). Open source, with CLAP since v2.11.
whyUnique: Models the physics of tape instead of just EQ-ing it.
bitwigTips: Use the CLAP build. Bitwig's Chain device lets you A/B different tape settings.

name: ChowMatrix
description: A delay that grows like a tree: you branch delay lines off each other into a network.
whyUnique: The delay network is a visual tree you build node by node.
bitwigTips: Put it on a Return and modulate its insanity control with a slow Bitwig LFO.

name: Surge XT
description: Open-source hybrid synth with many oscillator types, MSEG modulators and a deep FX section. The CLAP version is first-class.
whyUnique: The Surge team helped push the CLAP format. It's a strong match for Bitwig's per-voice modulation.
bitwigTips: Use the CLAP build for polyphonic modulation from Bitwig's modulators.

name: Zebralette 3
description: Free single-oscillator spin-off of Zebra 3. The oscillator is drawn and warped through spectral and geometric modes.
whyUnique: A free way into u-he's spectral and drawn oscillator design.
bitwigTips: u-he ships CLAP builds. Use them for note-expression and per-voice modulation in Bitwig.

name: Ruina
description: Distortion and wavefolding from a Eurorack company, ported to software.
whyUnique: Eurorack-style destruction designed by module makers.
bitwigTips: Pair it with Bitwig's Grid for a modular-style chain around it.

name: Sandman Pro
description: A delay that can freeze, 'sleep' and glitch its buffer, with a big modulation matrix.
whyUnique: Freezing and sleeping the buffer turns a delay into a performance instrument.
bitwigTips: Map Freeze to a Bitwig Button modulator for hands-on capture.

name: Wires
description: Emulates wire recorders, the pre-tape magnetic format, along with their particular artifacts.
whyUnique: Wire recording is an obscure medium that few other plugins model.
bitwigTips: Use on Bitwig's Pre-FX of an Instrument Layer to age one layer only.

name: Driftmaker
description: Disintegrates delays and loops into decaying drifts.
whyUnique: A small, characterful free tool from a boutique ambient studio.
bitwigTips: Long tails sit well on a Return. Automate feedback for decaying transitions.

name: chipsounds
description: Obsessively accurate emulation of 8-bit sound chips, down to the bugs.
whyUnique: Recreates each chip's individual quirks instead of generic square waves.
bitwigTips: Combine it with Bitwig's Arpeggiator at 1/32 for authentic chip arps.

name: Frohmage
description: Cult free resonant filter with a built-in sequencer and distortion.
whyUnique: An odd, rough filter that has been in producers' folders for decades.
bitwigTips: Pair it with Bitwig's Step modulator for an alternate filter sequence.

name: Playbeat
description: Generative groove engine that shuffles and remixes beat patterns with smart randomization.
whyUnique: Randomization designed to make musical sense, built to break you out of familiar patterns.
bitwigTips: Record its MIDI output into a Bitwig clip, then edit with Bitwig 6's clip aliases.

name: Playbox
description: Layers samples across chords with heavy randomization for unexpected combinations.
whyUnique: The dice do the composing: one button gives you a new layered chord kit.
bitwigTips: Feed it chords from Bitwig 6's global key signature so the progressions stay in key.

name: Serato Sample
description: Fast sample chopping with high-quality time and pitch stretching.
whyUnique: Pitch'n Time quality stretching makes sampling feel effortless.
bitwigTips: Bitwig's Sampler covers the basics. Serato wins on stretch quality.

name: XLN Life
description: Turns everyday sound recordings, including ones from your phone, into beats.
whyUnique: Starts from field recordings instead of a library. It bridges the mobile and desktop sections of this app.
bitwigTips: Record ideas on your phone, drop them in, and drag the beat into Bitwig as MIDI.

name: M-Clarity 2
description: AI-assisted dynamic resonance suppression.
whyUnique: A creative-cleanup tool that removes harshness automatically.
bitwigTips: Place it before granular effects to stop resonances building up.

name: Smooth Operator Pro
description: Intelligent spectral balancing that tames harsh frequencies as the signal changes.
whyUnique: Spectral balancing that is as easy to use as a single knob.
bitwigTips: Useful on resampled granular textures before printing.
